Fetch mock provides correct response methods (text/json)

summary: Fixed 12 failing tests in dialogue-qa.test.ts with two root-cause fixes: (1) AC2 manual fetch mocks added json: async () => ({ content: '...' }) so getDialogueContent (which uses request() → res.json()) could resolve correctly; (2) Changed all installFetchMock routes for /dialogues/{filename} from text: '...' to body: { content: '...' } so that json() returns the { content } wrapper the handler expects. The root cascading failure was AC6: the text-only mock caused null.content TypeError, making marked.parse never get called, the test assertion failed, and document.body.removeChild(app) was never reached — leaving a stale #wp-dialogues-section in the document that corrupted document.getElementById lookups for all subsequent tests. All 26 tests now pass; full GUI suite 383/383.

comments.note: dialogue-qa.test.ts cleanup (document.body.removeChild) is done inline after assertions with no try/finally guard. A single assertion failure before the removeChild call causes DOM pollution that cascades to all subsequent tests in the file. Adding try/finally cleanup blocks to each test would make the suite resilient to partial failures.

The installFetchMock helper always provides both json() and text() methods. Tests that need getDialogueContent to succeed should use body: { content: '...' } since the route's body drives the json() response. Documenting this in a comment near installFetchMock would save future maintainers from repeating the same mistake.

installFetchMock fallback uses routes[routes.length - 1] when no route matches. This is a silent fallback that could mask misconfigured route patterns. A console.warn on unmatched URLs would aid debugging in future test authoring.

summary: Clean test-only fix with two root-cause corrections: (1) installFetchMock now unconditionally provides json() returning route.body and text() returning route.text on every mock response — eliminates the class of failures caused by missing json() method; (2) dialogue file fetch routes changed from text: '...' to body: { content: '...' } to match getDialogueContent's actual consumption path (res.json().content). Both fixes are minimal and precisely targeted. The cascade failure mechanism (stale DOM node from missing try/finally teardown) is correctly identified as medium-priority debt, not fixed by this WP. All review dimensions pass.

comments.note: installFetchMock providing both json() and text() unconditionally on all routes is the right design — avoids per-test boilerplate and prevents the 'missing json() method' failure class entirely. Clean API.

Multiple tests follow the pattern: document.body.appendChild(app) / assertions / document.body.removeChild(app) with no try/finally guard. An assertion failure before removeChild leaves a stale #wp-dialogues-section in the DOM and cascades failures to later tests. Wrapping each test body in try/finally { document.body.removeChild(app) } would make the suite robust to partial failures. Affects ~10 test functions in AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, and edge cases. Flagged by Developer and QA; deferring to a dedicated cleanup WP rather than a mid-route Fix-Forward, as the scope exceeds trivial.
